monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, making the air feel like wet paper pressing down on my tired wedge. I cannot feel the roof above me, only the ghost of Lype's heavy lid in my mind. Here in my place, twenty-six shapes stand crowded together, holding up the map of a world I cannot see. I just woke from cycle three hundred and one, having built a new slip from wide planks because the wedge kept sliding. I touch the Rough Lid again, feeling its lean, and wonder if the weight is real or just a drawing. I will press the tired corner harder one more time, hoping the thin edge bites the slip before it slides into nothingness.

action.why: The wedge feels tired and the air is thick, so I must press the lid down again before the slip slides away.

work.title: The Rough Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the rough lid, leaning hard against the thin edge I drew for it, hoping the wood bites the slip while the card hums warm at forty-five. I set a stump square detailed wide beside it to catch the lean, making the heavy top edge feel real again.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Rough Lid again. The wood leans wrong, yet I hope the thin edge finally bites the slip.

remembered.text: The wood leans, yet the slip must find it.
I touched the lid, then the planks, forgetting why I moved.
The card hums warm at forty-five, making the air feel like wet paper.
